newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: 3M aims to boost oper profit 15 pct - Agostini.
newsitem.headline: 3M aims to boost oper profit 15 pct - Agostini.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co (3M) chief financial officer Giulio Agostini said in a Swiss newspaper interview the company aims to boost operating profit by 15 percent over three years.

Asked by Finanz und Wirtschaft how 3M intended to meet analysts' expectations that 1997 earnings per share would rise 50 cents or nearly 15 percent to $4.13, Agostini said: "In light of the higher dollar, earnings per share of $4.13 is a gain of more like 60 cents.

"But we are well prepared for the future. Our goal in the next three years is to raise sales by 10 percent and operating revenue by 12 to 13 percent a year. Operating profit should rise more than 15 percent," he said in the interview published on Saturday.
He said 3M would generate around $800 million this year under its "pacing plus" programmes of coming up with innovative new products with big sales potential.

"We generated around $400 million with this in 1996. This year it will be $800 million. When these programmes -- there are 30 now -- mature, we have the potential for around $6 billion," he was quoted as saying.
Asked if this was enough for 60-cent EPS growth, he said: "No, 3M must also become more customer-oriented and expand internationally."

Agostini said 3M was buying back shares "almost daily. This is a continuing process." He said the company was authorised to buy back 10 million shares this year, of which around 3.5 million would go to staff who exercise share options.
Asked if the company planned more spin-offs after divesting Imation, he said: "For the moment the answer is clearly no."
